description: Use this when the user asks what a company is worth, wants a valuation range, or is preparing to buy or sell and needs an indicative number. Returns Cape Partners' indicative valuation range, produced by its triangulated method — revenue multiple, EBITDA multiple, discounted cash flow, a conservative floor and a weighted triangulation — together with the method used, the assumptions it rests on and a data-quality note. It is indicative and non-binding: not an offer, an appraisal or investment advice, and it commits neither Cape nor any counterparty. Use the financials the user provides; do not estimate figures they did not give, and say so plainly if the range depends on assumptions you supplied.

business_model.description: The family model to value with, only if the user described the business: software_saas (recurring software), it_services (project or staffed services), hybrid (both). Stored lowercase.

company.description: What the user told you about the company, in their words.

ebitda_margin.description: EBITDA margin. 0.2 or 20 both mean 20%, only if stated.

geography.description: Country or region the user named, if any.

gross_margin_pct.description: Gross margin as a fraction (0.70 = 70%); 70 is also accepted. Only if stated.

growth_rate.description: Annual growth. 0.3 or 30 both mean 30%, only if stated.

nrr_pct.description: Net revenue retention as a fraction (1.15 = 115%); 115 is also accepted. Software/hybrid only. Only if the user stated it — never estimate it.

recurring_share_pct.description: Share of revenue that is recurring. Stored as a fraction (0.65); 65 is also accepted and converted. Only if stated.

revenue_eur.description: Revenue in euros, only if the user stated it. A string like "8M" is accepted.

sector.description: Sector the user named, if any.

top_customer_pct.description: Share of revenue from the largest customer as a fraction (0.25 = 25%); 25 is also accepted. Only if stated.

name: get_valuation

confidence_band_pct.description: Half-width of the returned range as a fraction of the headline (0.15 = +/-15%), so it always agrees with value_range_eur.

family_model.description: The family-model view of the same inputs, matching what the web app shows: ev, range_eur, confidence and score with reasons, implied_multiples, benchmark_position, contributions, inputs_echo, k_market and params vintage. null when the family model is off.

legacy_engine.description: DEPRECATED. The retired triangulation, kept one release for traceability. Do not quote it: the top-level headline is the family model.

method_dispersion_eur.description: min/max across the methods that produced a figure.

method_sources.description: Where each method figure came from: the multiple, the tier and the premiums, or the DCF parameters.

methods.description: Only the methods that produced a figure; see methods_omitted.

next_step.description: What to do with the figure: how a mandate on file turns an indicative value into a ranked, named shortlist.

qualification.description: What to ASK the user next: the quality fields this answer had to default (nrr, top_customer, gross_margin), what supplying them is worth in confidence points, and the sentence to use. Relay the questions; do not invent the answers.

valuation_status.description: abstained = Cape declines to provide a valuation; this is not a valuation of zero.

value_range_eur.description: The valuation RANGE, derived from how much is known: the half-width follows the confidence score (+/-15% at a perfect score, +/-22% at the HIGH/MEDIUM boundary, +/-45% at zero), never how far the methods disagree — see method_dispersion_eur. null when Cape abstains.

weights.description: The weights actually applied, after any redistribution.

title: Get an indicative company valuation
